questions.q: How does this lesson's handoff document differ in purpose from the Lesson 1 requirements checklist?
options: They serve exactly the same purpose and can be merged into one file
The checklist tracks whether the build is finished; the handoff document is written for whoever inherits the org next
The handoff document replaces the need for any testing
The checklist is for interviewers, and the handoff document is only for the original builder
questions.explain: The lesson draws this distinction directly: the Lesson 1 checklist is a build-completion tracker, while the handoff document is written for a successor -- a new hire, a consultant, or an interviewer.

questions.q: What four pieces of information does the Section 4 automation inventory record for every Flow, validation rule, and the approval process?
options: Owner, creation date, last modified date, and record count
Name, type/trigger, what it does, and why it exists
Object, field label, data type, and required/optional
Profile, role, OWD setting, and sharing rule
questions.explain: The lesson's four-line format is: Name, Type/Trigger, What it does, Why it exists -- applied consistently to every automation item.

questions.q: Which three things does Section 8 (Known Limitations) explicitly say this build does NOT include?
options: Reports, dashboards, and sample data
Role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules
Lightning Web Components, integration with an outside ERP/accounting system, and Apex
Validation rules, Flows, and an approval process
questions.explain: The lesson lists these three specifically, framing the build as intentionally, fully declarative -- consistent with Lesson 1's 'declarative build' definition.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson's artifact does the Data Model section of the handoff document pull from?
options: Lesson 17's test results
Lesson 3's object-relationship diagram
Lesson 16's sample data volumes
Lesson 14's approval process configuration
questions.explain: The Data Model section reuses the Lesson 3 object-relationship diagram plus a table of every custom field added since.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a list of automation with no "why" column is not useful to a successor?
options: Salesforce requires a "why" field on every Flow definition
Without knowing why something exists, the next administrator can't safely judge whether it's okay to change or remove it
The "why" column is only needed for validation rules, not Flows
It isn't useful -- the lesson recommends dropping the "why" column to save space
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames the 'why' as what lets a successor make a safe judgment call about changing or removing a piece of automation.
